newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean business groups offer aid to hungry North.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean business groups offer aid to hungry North.

text.p: South Korea's leading industrial conglomerates on Thursday joined a public effort to stave off famine in North Korea by pledging $2 million worth of corn.
The Federation of Korean Industries, which represents the country's largest companies, said in a statement the shipment of 11,000 tonnes of grain would be delivered through South Korea's Red Cross.
Its announcement came on the eve of Inter-Korean Red Cross talks in Beijing aimed at speeding up relief shipments.

"Our members agreed at a meeting that any support to our brethren in North Korea should be made on condition it contributes to improving South-North Korean relations and gives real help to North Korean citizens," the statement said.

South Korea's biggest industrial concerns, including the giant Samsung, Hyundai and Daewoo groups, are joining a growing wave of public sympathy in South Korea for the plight of fellow Koreans across the border.
There is little they can do to help by investing in the communist country because of severe restrictions imposed by Seoul on cross border contacts.
North Korea is teetering on the edge of famine following two consecutive years of devastating floods.
On Wednesday, South Korea's Red Cross said it would offer 1,000 tonnes of flour worth 350 million won ($392,000) during the meeting in Beijing.

The last round of talks on May 3 and 5 were also held in Beijing, but collapsed after the Northern side demanded to know the exact amount of aid it could expect. The South has since agreed to reveal the size of donations.
The South Korean Red Cross has proposed sending food directly to the North, instead of through the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.
It also wants to deliver aid through the land border at Panmunjom to cut transport costs. Aid is now sent by ship or by train through China.
On Tuesday, the South Korean Red Cross began delivering 15,000 tonnes of Chinese corn.
The Red Cross is the only legal channel for private aid from South Korea to the North.
Last Friday, the South Korean government pledged fresh food aid worth $10 million to a U.N. appeal for North Korea.

The promise of 50,000 tonnes of corn and 300 tonnes of powdered milk was on top of $6 million already delivered to the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), which has appealed for 200,000 tonnes of aid worth $98.5 million.
The United States has pledged $25 million to the WFP.
